assessment.reason: Projection sits modestly under the line and the direction survives the opportunity stress, but the offered -106 only just clears the model's minimum acceptable price, leaving almost no cushion.
assessment.model_case: A mean near 2.4 shots on 16.1 projected minutes sits just under 2.5, with a median of two. The weakness is a thin mean cushion. If Carolina's absences add ice time, volume drifts toward the line, though even the upward stress stays above break-even.
assessment.price_case: Main 2.5 line at -106 implies a break-even near 0.515, against a market near 0.53 across three books. Model fair odds are about -140, yet the price barely beats the roughly -107 minimum, so any adverse move erases the case.
assessment.context_case: The injury table is partial, with Boston coverage missing. Carolina absences may reshuffle forwards. Ehlers is quoted after a recent game, which does not confirm his workload. Exposure is correlated with the Svechnikov under in the same game.

qualitative_review.countercase: If Carolina's injury-driven lineup changes lift Ehlers into heavier top-six or power-play minutes, his shots could clear 2.5. The market already favors the under only modestly, and model calibration is unvalidated. BetOnline's own participation and overtime rules are assumed rather than checked.

findings.note: ESPN shows Ehlers with 26 shots on goal in 13 games this season, about 2.0 per game, and 2, 1, 4, 3 and 1 shots in his last five games. He plays about 16 minutes a night in a top-six role and on the No. 1 power-play unit.

The case against the Under: last season Ehlers had a career-best 26 goals and 71 points in the regular season, then 39 shots in 18 playoff games. Other CBS reporting says he had 207 regular-season shots, about 2.5 per game, which is right at this line.

Same-day game preview: Carolina has 20 points, and Boston has an eight-game point streak. Kochetkov and Swayman are the expected goalies. Ehlers mentioned teammates being out, but no injury news on him or a role change turned up.

Old (Feb 28, 2026): Cooley had 3 shots on goal against the Wild in a 5-2 win in only his second game back from a long-term lower-body injury, which beats the 2.5 line; this is not current reporting on the 2026-27 season.

Old (Oct 25, 2025): ESPN's play-by-play for the Mammoth's 6-2 win at Minnesota shows Cooley scoring twice and getting several other shots on Gustavsson, suggesting he has had more than 2.5 shots against the Wild before.

Old (Jan 2026): background on the left-knee/lower-body injury that kept Cooley out from Dec. 5, 2025 into late February; he played the rest of the season and the playoffs. I found no current injury, lineup or practice news for this game.
